stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Completed in 1932, the Orrin Valley Viaduct carried freight trains across a river gorge for almost ninety years. Its designers relied on an early form of reinforced concrete whose long-term behavior was not yet understood. By the time inspectors closed the viaduct in 2021, rainwater seeping through hairline cracks in the piers ______ much of the steel embedded inside them.
explanation: The time marker is "By the time inspectors closed the viaduct in 2021." The closing is a past event, and the corrosion happened before it. When one past action comes before another past action, you use the past perfect, so "had corroded" is correct.

A.why: You chose the present tense, but the passage describes a closing that already happened in 2021. The damage can't be happening now in a sentence set in the past.

B.why: You went with the simple past because the sentence has a date. But "by the time" means the corrosion came before the 2021 closing, and only "had corroded" shows that order.

D.why: You chose the future perfect, which describes something that will be finished at a future point. The closing in 2021 is in the past, so a future form doesn't fit.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In 2009, seismologist Idris Kalema installed forty sensors along the Tavish Fault, a 200-kilometer fracture in the region's bedrock. Since then, the network, which sends continuous readings to laboratories in three countries, ______ more than 12,000 small tremors, giving researchers an unusually detailed picture of how stress accumulates along the fault.
explanation: Look past the "which" clause and find the time marker, "Since then." "Since" describes an action that started in the past and is still going on, and that needs the present perfect. "Has recorded" is correct.

A.why: You picked the simple past because the passage opens with 2009. But "since then" means the recording runs from 2009 up to now, which calls for the present perfect, not the simple past.

C.why: You chose the past perfect, but there's no later past event for the recording to come before. The period described runs up to the present.

D.why: You chose the future tense, but "since then" points back to 2009. The tremors have already been recorded.

stimulus: The Sallow Aquifer supplies water to more than two hundred farms in the Keene Valley. When hydrologists began monitoring it in 2003, pumping for irrigation over the previous five decades ______ the aquifer's water table by nearly twelve meters, and several shallow wells had already run dry.
explanation: The monitoring began in 2003, and the pumping happened "over the previous five decades," which is before that past point. The parallel clause "had already run dry" is also in the past perfect. "Had lowered" shows the right order and matches that clause.

B.why: You chose the present tense, but the sentence is anchored to 2003 and to the fifty years before it. That's a past timeline, not the present.

C.why: You went with the simple past because of the date 2003. But "previous five decades" puts the pumping before the monitoring, and the parallel clause uses "had already run dry." Only the past perfect shows that earlier-past order.

D.why: You chose the future tense, but the lowering happened during the five decades before 2003. It is already finished.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Agronomists at the Keller Plains Research Farm are testing whether a mixture of clover and winter rye can restore nitrogen to depleted soil. The cover crops were sown last October in twelve trial plots. Next April, once the plots have been tilled, the team of agronomists and graduate students ______ soil samples from each plot and compare them with samples taken before planting.
explanation: The time marker is "Next April," so the action is in the future. The blank also pairs with the bare verb "compare," which only works after "will." "Will collect ... and compare" is correct.

A.why: You picked the simple past, maybe because of "last October" in the sentence before. But this sentence is set "Next April," which hasn't happened yet.

B.why: You chose the present perfect, which describes something already done. The sampling is planned for next April, so it can't be done yet.

C.why: You chose the simple present, but "Next April" calls for the future. "Collects" also doesn't pair with the bare verb "compare" that follows.

explanation: The time marker is "Since the beds were first described in 1986." "Since" describes work that started in the past and continues to now, which needs the present perfect. "Have identified" is correct.

A.why: You chose the simple past because of the date 1986. But "since" covers the whole stretch from 1986 to the present, which calls for the present perfect.

B.why: You chose the simple present, which describes a habit or a general truth. It can't express a total built up "since" a past date.

D.why: You chose the past perfect, but there's no later past event for the identifying to come before. The count runs up to the present.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Printmaker Mireille Aucoin carved the woodblock for Low Tide in 1974, using only three colors of ink. In the print, a solitary heron stands at the edge of a mudflat while a line of fishing boats ______ toward the horizon, their sails rendered as thin strips of pale blue.
explanation: When you describe what happens inside an artwork, you use the present tense. The parallel clause already does this with "a solitary heron stands." To match it, you need "drifts," which agrees with the singular subject "line."

B.why: You switched to the simple past because the print was made in 1974. But the scene inside the print is described in the present ("stands"), and the verb in the parallel clause has to match it.

C.why: You chose the past perfect, which would mean the boats drifted before some other past event. In the scene, the boats move at the same time the heron stands.

D.why: You chose the future tense, but the boats are drifting in the scene right now, at the same moment the heron "stands."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Kaleri, a language first documented in 2011 by linguist Ana Voskuijlen, is spoken in four villages in a mountain valley. Unlike English speakers, who often move a verb to the front of a sentence to ask a question, Kaleri speakers mark a yes-or-no question by raising the pitch of the final syllable, and they ______ the order of the words unchanged.
explanation: The sentence describes how Kaleri works in general, and the parallel clause uses the present tense: "Kaleri speakers mark." The verb joined to it by "and" should match, so "leave" is correct.

A.why: You chose the simple past because the passage mentions 2011. But that date is when the language was documented. How speakers form questions is an ongoing fact, stated in the present ("mark").

B.why: You chose the past perfect, but nothing in the sentence is a past event for this action to come before. The parallel verb "mark" is present.

C.why: You chose the future tense, but the sentence describes how speakers form questions now. The parallel verb "mark" is present, not future.
